executiveSummary: The only executable source in this repository is validate-codepulse.ps1, a 185-line PowerShell validation script. It is readable, flat, and fails fast with specific error messages; every top-level statement is within acceptable cyclomatic and cognitive thresholds.

Maintainability cost comes from repetition rather than difficulty: the same contains-or-throw guard is hand-written in 18 places, string comparisons are inconsistent, and the script stops at the first failure. A small data-driven helper would remove most of this accidental complexity.

overall.note: Weighted per complexity-model.md: Cyclomatic 98 x 10%, Cognitive 95 x 15%, Accidental 82 x 15%, Other quality signals 85 x 60% = 87.35.

excluded: Markdown skill and reference files (instructions, not code)

executedChecks: [System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile('validate-codepulse.ps1') AST decision-point count per top-level statement
notes: No functions are defined, so each top-level statement (30 non-trivial units) is treated as the measured unit.
Cyclomatic = 1 + if/elseif clauses + loops + -and/-or operators. Cognitive is a SonarSource-style estimate from the same AST (+1 per flow break, + nesting level).

assessments.summary: Readable, flat validation script with no complexity threshold breaches. Deductions come from duplicated guard logic, hardcoded skill inventory, inconsistent string comparison, and fail-fast reporting.

measures.note: Duplicated contains-or-throw guards; hardcoded skill counts and names

hotspots.note: Highest in file; within thresholds. Five independent checks share one loop body.

findings.title: Contains-or-throw guard duplicated 18 times

evidence.note: Same pattern for runtime contract, token efficiency, orchestration, setup doc, and benchmark plan

findings.impact: Each new contract rule requires copying a loop, guard, and message. Inconsistencies (see QUAL-001) creep in because each copy is written independently.
findings.recommendation: Inherent-vs-accidental test: the same behavior can be expressed more simply. Replace with one helper, e.g. Assert-Contains -Path <file> -Items <string[]> -Label <text> [-IgnoreCase], driven by a table of file-to-required-text entries.

findings.title: Skill inventory hardcoded in three places
findings.impact: Adding or removing a skill requires editing magic numbers and an exclusion list that duplicate the skillName enum in codepulse-report-schema.json.
findings.recommendation: Derive the expected skill list from the skillName enum in codepulse-shared/schemas/codepulse-report-schema.json and compare sets, instead of hardcoding counts and names.

findings.title: Inconsistent string comparison semantics

evidence.note: IndexOf without StringComparison (culture-sensitive, case-sensitive) also at lines 55, 61, 68, 71, 76, 82, 125, 129, 131, 137, 141
IndexOf with OrdinalIgnoreCase also at lines 151, 167, 168, 175, 180

findings.impact: Readers must check each call to know whether a rule is case-sensitive. Culture-sensitive IndexOf can behave differently across locales.
findings.recommendation: Use one comparison policy: StringComparison.Ordinal for exact contract text, OrdinalIgnoreCase only where intentional. Centralize it in the QUAL-ACC-001 helper.

findings.title: Validation stops at the first failure
findings.impact: Contributors fixing a broad change (such as this report migration) must rerun the script once per defect.
findings.recommendation: Collect failures into a list, print all of them, and exit 1 when any exist.

findings.title: Flat, readable structure with specific failure messages

evidence.note: Schema checks parse JSON with ConvertFrom-Json rather than text matching

findings.impact: Every rule reads top to bottom with at most two nesting levels, and each failure names the file and missing item.
findings.recommendation: Preserve this property when introducing the QUAL-ACC-001 helper.

limitations: No PowerShell complexity analyzer (PSScriptAnalyzer) was installed; cognitive values are estimates and lizard does not support PowerShell.
Change frequency and test coverage were not assessed; the repository has no automated tests for the validator itself.

topRisks.summary: Main driver of maintenance effort as contract rules grow.

recommendations.title: Introduce a data-driven Assert-Contains helper
recommendations.detail: Collapse the 18 guards into a table of file-to-required-text entries with one comparison policy. Small effort.

recommendations.title: Derive skill inventory from the report schema
recommendations.detail: Remove hardcoded counts and exclusion lists. Small effort.

recommendations.title: Report all validation failures in one run
recommendations.detail: Accumulate errors and exit non-zero at the end. Small effort.

limitations: Static review of a single script; Markdown instruction files were not scored as code.
Cognitive complexity is an AST-assisted manual estimate.
conclusion: Code quality is good (B, 87). The validator is easy to read; consolidating its repeated guard pattern is the single highest-value improvement.
